t: A RISC-V developer kit with eight AI cores for running language models at home.
steps: Buy the BPI-SM10 kit from the BPI Shop or ameriDroid. Pick the memory size you need.
Get a 12 V 5 A or 19 V 2.37 A barrel power supply and a USB to serial cable.
Add an M.2 E-key Wi-Fi card or use the Ethernet port.
Install SpacemiT's Titan flashing tool on a Windows or Linux PC.
Follow the Banana Pi getting started guide to flash the Bianbu Linux image.
Boot the board and log in over the serial cable or a monitor.
Try a small language model demo, then move up to bigger ones.
meta: Open Board. From $370. A few stores.
